foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state will remain elevated near 72% over the next 30 days, driven by sustained gas supply stress (71% pressure, 79% state confirmation) and 7 urgent critical...
foil.perspective_strategic: The 71% pressure and 79% state confirmation indicate a structurally reinforced energy repricing path through gas supply stress, but the absence of directly matched reporting caps confidence at 75%, suggesting the market is pricing in disruption without full confirmation.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The contrarian case is supported by the 'Alternative Routes for Middle East Oil and Gas' headline and the fact that only 1 clustered situation and 1 linked forecast feed the canonical state path, meaning the disruption may be more localized than systemic, allowing stabilization if no new hard signals emerge.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 72%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through gas supply stress, with 71% pressure and 79% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
